1	# LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon
2	
3	LeanAG Horizon is a multi-project Lean 4 and Mathlib workspace for formalizing algebraic
4	geometry with [Archon Horizon](https://github.com/frenzymath/Archon-Horizon). Its central goal is
5	the algebraic-geometry version of the [Algebraic Jacobian challenge](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian.20challenge/near/587802685),
6	proposed by Christian Merten after Kevin Buzzard's differential-geometry challenge.
7	
8	> [!IMPORTANT]
9	> The workspace develops **two live routes** to the Algebraic Jacobian challenge. Follow the
10	> project named by the active task rather than treating either route as reference-only.
11	>
12	> - `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` continues the ambitious Picard-scheme route, building
13	>   representability by the Milne–Kollár construction of `Pic^r`, then `Pic^0` and the Albanese
14	>   property. Its Grassmannian, graded-algebra and flattening-stratification substrate is sorry-free
15	>   and still consumed, but the Quot-scheme endgame it was first written for is not the path being
16	>   built. Since 2026-07-28 its headline is stated over an arbitrary base field, with
17	>   representability asked of the étale-sheafified Picard functor and no rational-point hypothesis.
18	> - `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` develops a cleaner curve-specialized route
19	>   from protected target statements.
20	
21	The two projects share mathematical sources and supporting subprojects while keeping independent
22	Lean roots, blueprints, and roadmaps. The rebuild is listed first in the workspace manifest as the
23	default project; explicitly scoped tasks may and do advance the ambitious original route.
24	
25	The [live dashboard](https://axeldlv00.github.io/LeanAlgebraicGeometry/) is the best view of current
26	tasks, commits, session logs, blueprint graphs, and declaration-level progress. A static snapshot
27	is published approximately every 30 minutes; GitHub Pages deployment and caching can add a few
28	minutes before a new snapshot is visible.
29	
30	## Repository Layout
31	
32	| Path | Role |
33	| --- | --- |
34	| `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` | Cleaner curve-specialized AJC route and workspace default. |
35	| `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` | Ambitious Picard-scheme AJC route (Milne–Kollár representability), maintained by scoped tasks. |
36	| `SubProjects/` | Supporting, extracted, and related-paper formalizations available to the active project. |
37	| `references/` | Shared mathematical sources and retrieval notes. |
38	| `.archon-horizon/` | Workspace state: tasks, roadmap, inbox, run metadata, graphs, and ledger. |
39	| `config.yaml` | Ordered workspace manifest. The rebuild is listed first because it is the primary project. |
40	
41	Each route has its own overview:
42	
43	- [`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/README.md`](MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/README.md)
44	- [`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/README.md`](MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/README.md)
45	
46	## Project Map
47	
48	The workspace currently registers these projects, in priority order:
49	
50	| Project | Purpose |
51	| --- | --- |
52	| **`Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`** | Cleaner curve-specialized route; default project in the workspace manifest. |
53	| `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` | Ambitious Picard-scheme, `Pic^0`, and Albanese route. |
54	| `Line-Bundle-Comparison-Iso` | Extracted line-bundle pullback, tensor, and dual comparison infrastructure. |
55	| `Albanese` | Albanese universal property, rigidity, and rational-map-extension infrastructure. |
56	| `Cech-Cohomology` | Čech computation of higher direct images and its cohomological substrate. |
57	| `GR-Quot-Closure` | Relative Grassmannian and quotient-representability infrastructure. |
58	| `MR0555258-Compactifying-Picard` | Compactifying the Picard scheme (D'Souza), under `SubProjects/RelatedPapersFormalisation/`. |
59	| `Picard-IdentityComponent` | Extracted Picard identity-component and `Pic^0` development. |
60	
61	These member projects remain useful sources of proved APIs, mathematical designs, and failure
62	memory for both main routes.
63	
64	## Working in a Main Project
65	
66	The workspace currently uses Lean and Mathlib `v4.31.0`. Build the project named by the task. For
67	the ambitious Picard-scheme route:
68	
69	```bash
70	cd MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge
71	lake build
72	```
73	
74	The rebuild uses the shared workspace package directory at `.lake-packages`, so member projects
75	can reuse the same Mathlib checkout while retaining independent build directories.
76	
77	For workspace-wide exploration, run commands from the repository root:
78	
79	```bash
80	horizon dashboard
81	horizon graph -p Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge frontier
82	horizon search "Jacobian Picard representability"
83	```
84	
85	The first command starts the local dashboard. The graph command shows the ranked proof frontier
86	for the active project, and search queries declarations across the workspace and Mathlib.
87	
88	Treat `graph frontier` output as advisory and verify each row in the tree: neither main project has
89	an `hgraph/config.yaml`, so `horizon graph … sync` is a no-op and the stored graph drifts behind
90	landed work (archived inbox item `I-0501`). The scanner also invents declarations from docstring
91	prose, and some arrive marked `sorry`, so the frontier can list nodes that do not exist (archived
92	`I-0472`). Both defects were reproduced and neither was fixed.
93	
94	## Methodology
95	
96	[Archon Horizon](https://github.com/frenzymath/Archon-Horizon) coordinates long-running
97	formalization while keeping mathematical and operational state explicit:
98	
99	- **Horizon sessions** implement and verify Lean proofs against concrete tasks.
100	- **Fresh-context reviewers** such as Ground, work-reviewer, and janitor are dispatched at review
101	  and maintenance checkpoints rather than acting as a permanent second driver.
102	- **Blueprint graphs (`hgraph`)** track declaration dependencies, proof status, comments, and the
103	  ranked frontier for each project.
104	- **Roadmap, tasks, and inbox** record strategy, scoped work, cross-session handoffs, and durable
105	  failure memory.
106	- **The workspace ledger** records coherent commits and powers the public dashboard's progress
107	  and session views.
108	
109	Concurrent sessions can share a project's root import file. When adding one
110	import, build the staged root from the ledger's current `HEAD` and insert only
111	that line; do not stage the whole on-disk root, which may contain another
112	session's uncommitted imports.
113	
114	The mathematical blueprint is kept separate from implementation journals. Lean-specific progress
115	and failed approaches belong in graph comments, tasks, or the inbox, while the blueprint remains a
116	timeless account of the mathematics.
117	
118	## Contributing
119	
120	Contributions are welcome, but keep the two routes and task scope explicit:
121	
122	- **AJC proofs and infrastructure:** change only the main project named by the task; share reusable
123	  inputs through the supporting projects when appropriate.
124	- **Protected statements:** do not alter the signatures in the rebuild's `Challenge.lean` or files
125	  covered by `archon-protected.yaml` without prior agreement. Contributions should discharge those
126	  statements, not weaken or reshape them silently.
127	- **Issues and discussions:** include the declaration name and file path, and state whether the
128	  question concerns the statement, naming, proof strategy, or intended use.
129	- **Large changes:** check the live dashboard or open an issue first so work does not duplicate an
130	  active Horizon task.
131	- **Supporting work:** a focused subproject under `SubProjects/` is appropriate when a reusable
132	  dependency needs to be developed independently, but its intended consumer should be the active
133	  rebuild.
134	
135	Clear, stable, mathematical declaration names and warning-free builds are expected. Using the
136	`horizon` CLI is recommended so contributions remain aligned with the workspace manifest,
137	blueprint graph, and ledger conventions.

1	# Algebraic Jacobian Challenge
2	
3	A Lean 4 formalization of the Jacobian of a smooth, proper, geometrically
4	irreducible curve over a field.  The project takes the Picard-scheme route: build
5	the relative Picard functor, represent it, identify its identity component as an
6	abelian variety of dimension the genus, and derive the Albanese universal
7	property.  The first and last legs are substantially built; representability is
8	the open frontier.
9	
10	Representability is being built by the **Milne–Kollár route** — construct
11	`Pic^r` over a separably closed field from the loci where `h⁰ = 1`, glue,
12	descend to `k` by a finite Galois quotient, assemble the degrees by a coproduct.
13	The plan of record is [`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`](informal/pic-representability-campaign.md).
14	The Grothendieck/Kleiman quotient route via the Quot scheme is **not** the path
15	being built: its descent step needs a quasi-projectivity hypothesis that is not
16	expressible at the pinned Mathlib revision and without which the lemma is false.
17	Its substrate (Grassmannians, graded algebra, flattening stratification) is
18	sorry-free and is consumed by the committed route, so it is retained.
19	
20	Two of the committed route's own engines are substantially built.  The rigidified
21	pushforward gate is **discharged**: `Adelic.instHasRigidPushforwardOfCurve` is a real
22	instance for every curve satisfying the challenge hypotheses, and it measures axiom-clean
23	at the synthesis site, as do the three extraction theorems that now synthesise it rather
24	than assuming it.  The finite Galois
25	quotient has Speiser descent, the affine quotient, and `Γ`-stable affine covers proved;
26	what remains there is gluing.  Both are stated with proofs and Lean pins in the
27	blueprint's FGA chapter, §"The Milne–Kollár route".  Neither route is hypothesis-free:
28	the quotient route needs quasi-projectivity of the Abel-map slice, the committed route
29	needs every finite Galois orbit to lie in an affine open, and the same Hironaka example
30	defeats both if its hypothesis is dropped.  The difference is that the orbit condition is
31	available for the schemes this route quotients.
32	
33	It is developed alongside `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`, which attacks the
34	same theorem by a separate curve-specialized strategy.
35	
36	## State (measured 2026-07-30)
37	
38	- **361 modules, 191,855 lines** (re-measured 2026-07-31 by the recipe below, up from
39	  312/173,191 the previous day — the tree grew 49 modules in one day of parallel-lane work,
40	  so any figure quoted here is stale within hours).  The `sorry`
41	  count is deliberately not restated here: parallel lanes land work continuously, and a
42	  comment-stripped census is the only honest way to take it.  These counts move whenever a
43	  module lands, so re-measure rather
44	  than quoting them:
45	
46	  ```bash
47	  find AlgebraicJacobian -name '*.lean' | wc -l          # modules on disk
48	  find AlgebraicJacobian -name '*.lean' -exec cat {} + | wc -l
49	  lake build AlgebraicJacobian 2>&1 | grep -c 'declaration uses .sorry'
50	  ```
51	- **Rootedness is worth measuring, not assuming.**  A module that nothing imports
52	  compiles green and is invisible *both* to the root build and to the axiom probe,
53	  with nothing warning about it — `import AlgebraicJacobian` never reaches it, so no
54	  `#print axioms` line for it can even be written.  The check is the second
55	  measurement in [`scripts/axiom-frontier.lean`](scripts/axiom-frontier.lean)'s
56	  header.  Modules land here from several parallel efforts, so the unrooted set is
57	  routinely non-empty for a short while: a module not yet committed to the workspace
58	  ledger must **not** be rooted, since a clean checkout would then fail to build.  That
59	  grace period ends at the commit — once a module is in the ledger, leaving it unrooted
60	  means the build does not check it.  **Currently violated in 4 modules** (re-measured
61	  2026-07-31 by walking `import AlgebraicJacobian` transitively from the root module: 357
62	  of 361 in the root cone, 4 outside it): `Cohomology/CechTwistedCoherenceReductionProof`,
63	  `Picard/DivGrassmannianEmbedding`, `RiemannRoch/Ledger/FiberCoordinateComplex`,
64	  `RiemannRoch/Ledger/UniformRiemannRoch`.  All 4 are at ledger `HEAD`, so none is inside
65	  the grace period.  The 40-file `RiemannRoch/Ledger` cone that earlier measurements
66	  flagged has since been rooted (its issue `I-0600` is closed), so this is no longer one
67	  lane's port: the remainder is scattered across three areas.
68	
69	  The count has moved 6 → 14 → 18 → 19 → 20 → 4 over six measurements, in both directions;
70	  re-measure rather than quoting, and walk imports transitively rather than reading the
71	  root's import lines.  Declarations in these
72	  modules are not elaborated by `lake build AlgebraicJacobian`, and no `#print axioms`
73	  line through the root can reach them.  Use the reachability snippet in
74	  [`scripts/axiom-frontier.lean`](scripts/axiom-frontier.lean)'s header, seeded at
75	  `AlgebraicJacobian` rather than `AlgebraicJacobian.Jacobian`.

85	  synthesise the instance.  Run

87	  scripts/axiom-frontier.lean`; the probe carries **215** `#print axioms` lines as of

5	## Project
6	
7	A **from-scratch rebuild** of the Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization of the **Jacobian of a smooth,
8	proper, geometrically irreducible curve** over a field (Christian Merten's AI challenge, inspired by
9	Kevin Buzzard's Riemann-surface version). By a smooth curve we mean a geometrically irreducible,
10	smooth scheme of relative dimension one over a field.
11	
12	This project supplies the missing definitions (`genus`, `Jacobian`, the Abel–Jacobi map `ofCurve`)
13	and theorems (the Jacobian is smooth of relative dimension equal to the genus, proper, geometrically
14	irreducible, and is the Albanese variety of the curve, characterized by the universal property
15	`exists_unique_ofCurve_comp`). It targets the **extended** challenge: additionally, the Jacobian is
16	**functorial** in the curve (`Jacobian.functor`) and **commutes with base change of fields**
17	(`baseChangeIso` with identity and cocycle coherences, and Abel–Jacobi compatibility
18	`baseChange_ofCurve`), which makes the construction canonical.
19	
20	It is rebuilt rather than continued: the goal is a cleaner, more general, mathlib-idiomatic
21	infrastructure and a shorter, clearer path to the conclusion. The existing project
22	`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` may be **read** when genuinely blocked, but nothing is
23	copied from it — every declaration is rewritten. The rebuild is driven by its Archon Horizon task,
24	which carries the full charter (target, constraints, working model, and phases).

29	  reviewer must trust, and nothing else. Agents own the proofs, never these signatures.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Is every blueprint `\leanok` honest?  Run from the project root:
#
#   scripts/leanok-audit.sh
#
# A `\leanok` is a LOCAL mark, but the defect it can hide is TRANSITIVE: a proof
# genuinely written in Lean is still not proved if it routes through a `sorry`, and
# nothing at the mark says so.  So the marks have to be joined against the axioms of
# the declarations they pin.  Reading cannot answer this question; that is the whole
# reason this script exists.
#
# Two positions, two different claims, measured SEPARATELY:
#
#   * a PROOF-level mark says the proof is formalised.  One on a `sorryAx` carrier is
#     a DEFECT.  Expected count: 0.
#   * a STATEMENT-level mark says the signature is formalised, which is TRUE of a
#     `sorry`-bodied declaration.  One on a `sorryAx` carrier is LEGITIMATE and must
#     NOT be "fixed".  Expected count: 34 and growing, as the open chapters take
#     landings.
#
# THE RECONCILIATION IDENTITY IS THE CHECK.  `public + private + unresolved == pins`
# is asserted per position, in code, and the script fails on a shortfall.  Six
# separate domain-shrinking bugs have been found in this audit, each of which printed
# a plausible `0 defects` line while examining a strict subset:
#
#   1. `#print axioms` on an absent name is an error and `lean` halts at 100 of them,
#      truncating the audit silently.  (Gone: `collectAxioms` returns a value.)
#   2. an output log matched by its own input glob and re-ingested as a batch.
#   3. a parser anchored on the closing quote of `'<name>'`, dropping every name
#      containing an apostrophe -- 49 pins do.
#   4. `#print axioms` printing `does not depend on any axioms`, a DIFFERENT sentence
#      that a `depends on axioms: [...]` regex never matches.
#   5. `split` numbering past `az` to `ba`, so a `lk_a*` glob skipped 33 pins.
#   6. `re.search` keeping only the FIRST `\lean{}` macro of a statement; two nodes in
#      `Picard_QuotScheme.tex` carry several, worth 8 pins.
#
# Only #5 and #6 were caught by the assertion after it was in place -- each had
# survived a careful reading of the code first.  #6 was found by chasing a DOMAIN
# disagreement (1552 vs 1560) against a second extractor that already AGREED on the
# answer (34): when two independent measurements agree on the finding and differ on
# how much they looked at, the gap is the thing to chase, because domain size is
# exactly what the false clean lines were wrong about.
#
# Two design points that are not incidental:
#
#   * environments are matched with an explicit STACK, not a non-greedy regex.  A
#     regex reaches past the true `\end{theorem}` whenever anything intervenes, and
#     that silently pairs one node's statement with a LATER node's proof.  It was the
#     entire source of three retracted "dishonest mark" findings.
#   * axioms come from `Lean.collectAxioms`, not `#print axioms`.  The latter resolves
#     through the EXPORTED environment, so a `private` constant is unaddressable from
#     outside its defining file; the former runs against `setExporting false` and
#     decides all of them.  188 statement-level pins are private.  "My probe cannot
#     see it" is a fact about the probe.
#
# The private lane carries a POSITIVE CONTROL, without which "zero private pins carry
# sorryAx" is indistinguishable from a lane measuring nothing: exactly one private pin
